newsitem.title: UK: UK's Redwood sets "Labour bad for firms" campaign.
newsitem.headline: UK's Redwood sets "Labour bad for firms" campaign.

text.p: Britain's Conservatives on Tuesday launched their first major campaign since going into opposition, blaming the Labour government for hurting business through soaring sterling, higher taxes and new laws.

Launching the "Labour's bad for business" campaign, shadow trade and industry spokesman John Redwood told a news conference: "The brunt of adjustment is falling very strongly on those who make things and those who dare to try to export things."
He said this month's budget had seen "a series of undesirable measures which have hit the corporate sector but done nothing about the consumer boom".

Redwood repeated charges that sterling had become a "one-way bet for the markets" because the budget had forced interest rates higher, but said higher rates and higher sterling were just two aspects of the Labour government's assault on business.

Others included the windfall tax on privatised utilities, the ending of tax relief for company pension funds, the signing of the European Union social chapter, the plan for a minimum wage and new "moral" policies on aid and on arms sales.

Redwood said he and his colleagues in the Conservative industry team would spend the parliamentary summer break which begins on Friday touring the country to find out in detail about the impact of such measures on individual companies.
